issues.t: Automatic transmission slipping or failing
issues.sym: Shifts that slip, flare or bang, a delay before the van moves, no reverse, or a sudden loss of drive with the engine still running. Failures often come with little warning.
issues.why: The four-speed automatic in the Freestar wears out internally, and failure is by far the most-reported problem on this van. Most owners report it somewhere around 90,000 to 120,000 miles.
issues.next: If shifting changes at all, have the fluid level and condition checked and the codes read right away. Slipping or no-drive usually means a rebuilt or replacement transmission, so get a written quote and compare it with the value of the van.

issues.t: Torque converter can fail and cut power (recall)
issues.sym: The van suddenly loses drive power while moving, often with no warning first.
issues.why: The output shaft of the torque converter (the fluid coupling between engine and transmission) can break. Ford recalled 2004 and 2005 Freestars to replace the torque converter.
issues.next: Run your VIN through Ford or NHTSA to see whether the recall was done. If not, call a Ford dealer to schedule the free torque converter replacement.

issues.t: Third-row seat anchor can rust loose (recall)
issues.sym: The third-row seat may not latch firmly, may rattle, or may shift. In a rear crash an unlatched seat raises injury risk.
issues.why: The sheet metal under the floor that holds the third-row seat latch strikers can corrode, especially in states that use road salt.
issues.next: Check for open recalls with your VIN and have a Ford dealer inspect and repair the seat mounting area for free. Avoid seating passengers in the third row until it is checked.

issues.t: Engine computer damaged by water leaks
issues.sym: Stalling or rough running, flickering dash or interior lights, battery light on, the radio or A/C cutting in and out, or the transmission acting up, often after rain or a car wash.
issues.why: Water can get past the cowl and windshield area seals and reach the powertrain control module (the main engine and transmission computer), which then fails or acts erratically.
issues.next: Have a shop check for water at the computer and its connectors and fix the leak path and water shield first. A damaged computer usually has to be replaced and programmed to the van.

issues.t: Rocker panel, door and subframe rust
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or holes along the rocker panels, door bottoms and wheel wells, a rusted liftgate latch, or heavy scale on the subframe underneath.
issues.why: The Freestar is built on the old Windstar platform and rusts in the same places, especially where roads are salted.
issues.next: Have the underbody and subframe inspected on a lift, especially before buying one. Cosmetic rust can be patched, but a badly rusted subframe is a safety problem.

issues.t: Misfire from a failing ignition coil pack
issues.sym: The engine shakes, runs rough or lacks power, and the check engine light may flash.
issues.why: The coil pack that feeds the spark plug wires fails with age and heat, often along with worn plugs and wires. An ongoing misfire can also upset shifting.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read and fix the misfire promptly. Replacing the coil pack, plugs and wires together is common.

issues.t: Misfire from clogged EGR ports in the intake
issues.sym: Rough idle or misfire codes on higher-mileage vans, sometimes on one or two cylinders only.
issues.why: Small passages in the intake manifold that carry exhaust gas (EGR) to each cylinder can clog with carbon sludge, so cylinders get uneven mixtures.
issues.next: Ask the shop to check the EGR passages before replacing coils or injectors. Cleaning them is often the fix.

issues.t: Squealing camshaft synchronizer
issues.sym: A screech or squeal from the engine that sounds like a bad belt, sometimes with stalling at stops.
issues.why: The camshaft synchronizer (the unit that holds the cam sensor) has a bearing that wears out. If it seizes it can damage the engine.
issues.next: Do not ignore a new screeching noise. Have the synchronizer checked and replaced if it is noisy or has play.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing whine or hum
issues.sym: A whistle, whine or hum from the front that changes with speed and may get louder in turns.
issues.why: Front hub bearings wear out. Ford issued bulletins about whistling and noise from the front hub bearings on these vans.
issues.next: Have the wheel bearings checked for play and noise. Replace the worn hub assembly before it gets loose.

issues.t: Cracked wheel hubs or rotors (recall)
issues.sym: Noise or looseness at a wheel. In the worst case a wheel can separate from the van.
issues.why: Some 2004 Freestars had wheel hubs, rotors or bearings that could crack. Ford recalled them for replacement.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have a Ford dealer do the free repair.

issues.t: Power steering line can come loose (recall)
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaking, smoke from under the hood, or a burning smell.
issues.why: A power steering line on some 2004 vans could disconnect and spray fluid on the hot exhaust, which can cause smoke or a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls. If you see smoke or smell burning fluid, pull over and shut the engine off.

issues.t: Power liftgate can drop suddenly (recall)
issues.sym: The power liftgate drifts down or falls when open.
issues.why: A strut on the power liftgate could fail on some 2005-2006 vans, so the gate would not stay up.
issues.next: Check your VIN for open recalls and have the free repair done. Until then, do not stand under an open liftgate.

issues.t: ABS and traction control lights on
issues.sym: The ABS, traction control and parking brake lights flicker or stay on, and traction control may stop working.
issues.why: Ford issued several bulletins for these lights, including a pressure sensor fault in the ABS system and module calibration faults. Owners also report failed ABS/traction control modules.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal braking still works, but ABS and traction control may not until the fault is fixed.

issues.t: Rear brakes wear fast or calipers seize
issues.sym: Rear pads and rotors wearing out early, grinding, or a hot, dragging rear wheel.
issues.why: Ford issued bulletins for fast rear brake lining wear on the Freestar, and owners report rear calipers that freeze up.
issues.next: Have the rear brakes checked at every oil change. Clean and lube the caliper slides at each brake job and replace a seized caliper.

issues.t: Power sliding door or liftgate will not open
issues.sym: The power sliding doors or power liftgate stop working from the overhead buttons or the key fob.
issues.why: Ford published bulletins on power sliding door and liftgate faults, including a module fault code that stops them responding.
issues.next: Have the door system codes read. Sometimes a reset or reprogram fixes it; otherwise a motor, cable or latch needs replacing.

issues.t: Alternator stops charging
issues.sym: Battery light on, dim lights, or a dead battery that keeps coming back.
issues.why: Owners report alternator failures, sometimes more than once.
issues.next: Have the battery and charging system tested before replacing parts.

issues.t: A/C compressor fails
issues.sym: The A/C blows warm, the compressor is noisy, or the A/C belt breaks.
issues.why: Owners report replaced A/C compressors, sometimes with a broken belt that also left the van unable to run.
issues.next: If the compressor is noisy or the belt breaks, have it checked before driving far. A seized compressor can take out the belt.

issues.t: Power steering leak or hard steering
issues.sym: Power steering fluid leaks, whining from the pump, or steering that feels heavy or slow to return to center.
issues.why: Owners report leaking power steering pumps, lines and racks on these vans.
issues.next: If the steering suddenly turns heavy, grip the wheel with both hands, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — have it towed and checked. Check the fluid level and look for leaks. Have the leak source found before the pump runs dry.

issues.t: Broken outer CV joint
issues.sym: Clicking when turning, a clunk from a front wheel, or a vibration on acceleration.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin on broken outer CV joints on Freestars built before May 2005. Owners also report clunks from the driveline.
issues.next: Have the front axles and boots checked. A broken CV joint can leave the van unable to move.

issues.t: Rear defroster and antenna stop working
issues.sym: Rear window defroster lines do not clear, and radio reception may be weak.
issues.why: The connector tab on the rear glass can come loose. Ford published repair bulletins for it.
issues.next: A shop can re-attach the tab with a repair kit. Replacing the glass is rarely needed.

issues.t: Front power windows stop working
issues.sym: A front window will not go up or down.
issues.why: Ford issued a bulletin for front window motors that stop working on these vans.
issues.next: Have the switch and motor tested. Usually the motor or regulator gets replaced.
